tagline: Eleven miles along the clay bluffs above Escambia Bay.
intro: Past Perry Avenue in Pensacola, US 90 takes the name Scenic Highway, narrows to two lanes and turns north along the west side of Escambia Bay. For 11 miles it runs along the bluffs, which the state calls the highest points on Florida's coastline. Families picnic at Gaberonne, and lovers, by the state's own account, watch the moon rise from Bay Bluffs Park above the bay.
There is clay in the ground here, once used for making bricks. Don Tristan de Luna came along this shore in 1559, and one of his ships has lain sunk offshore ever since.

moments.title: Chimney Park
moments.text: On Red Bluff a lone chimney is all that is left of an 1854 steam sawmill, destroyed on Braxton Bragg's orders in 1862 so the Union could not use it.

moments.title: Escambia River
moments.text: The scenic road ends in tidal wetlands where US 90 bridges the Escambia River, a crossing where drivers waited up to two hours after Hurricane Ivan washed out the I-10 bridge in 2004.

sources.label: Florida Scenic Highways, Pensacola Scenic Bluffs Highway
